title: One press applied twice when its request is delivered twice

source.says: the census's reading: caller intent identifiers differ from hashes of equal arguments, and idempotency needs a defined scope and atomic recording (S13); Stripe's API keys every POST by an idempotency key (S14). ADR-0154 adds RFC 9110 §9.2.2: a client must not retry a non-idempotent request automatically unless it knows the request is idempotent

claim: ADR-0154 (a command a page's handler calls declares `idempotent_by`, PW0338); ADR-0121 (every press has an interaction)

repro.how: no change at all: ADR-0120's store, whose Add is a Server Action in a `<form action>` as Next.js's docs write one, adds once per delivery of its request. The repair is T08's reference: an interaction id made per press, carried by the request, and applied once by the server

pleris.faithful: The same store, its Add's command without `idempotent_by`, as the Next.js action has no key: refused. Its neighbour is the store as it is, `idempotent_by InteractionId`, and the runtime test shows that neighbour adding once when its request is delivered twice.
pleris.mechanism: ADR-0121's interaction per press, applied once

test.name: T08's hidden test on the Pleris store with `idempotent_by` (bench.mjs, replay:reference)
test.command: node benchmarks/harness/bench.mjs run --task T08 --stack pleris --agent replay:reference
